title: Towards Cost-Effective Real-Time High-Throughput End Station Design for Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN)
problem: Achieving TSN compatibility on end stations with constrained resources, particularly on commodity hardware (COTS), while maintaining predefined communication schedules for deterministic real-time packet processing.
motivation: TSN is increasingly deployed in mission- and safety-critical industrial applications requiring deterministic high-throughput communications, but existing solutions are either expensive hardware-centric designs or incompatible with COTS hardware.
method: The design leverages DPDK to achieve ultra-low latency and nanosecond-level transmission accuracy for packet processing. A novel multi-core scheduling framework distributes real-time TSN traffic across processor cores to boost throughput. The software-based approach runs on standard COTS hardware without requiring specialized hardware acceleration. Performance is validated through a prototype integrated into a real-world TSN testbed.
key_novelty: A software-based multi-core scheduling framework that enables high-throughput, low-latency TSN packet processing on cost-effective commodity hardware.
contributions: Software-based TSN end station with ultra-low latency and nanosecond-level transmission accuracy via DPDK
Novel multi-core scheduling framework for real-time TSN traffic throughput optimization
Open-source implementation leveraging COTS hardware for cost-effectiveness
Comprehensive real-world testbed validation demonstrating practical viability
primary_theme: Software-based real-time networking on commodity hardware
